CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

AEME (Aquatic Ecosystem Model Ensemble) is an R package (roxygen2 markdown, testthat 3e, Language: en-GB) that builds inputs for, runs, and post-processes four 1D lake models behind one interface: DYRESM-CAEDYM (dy_cd), GLM-AED (glm_aed), GOTM-WET (gotm_wet) and Simstrat-AED2 (simstrat_aed2). Model executables are not bundled; they are fetched with install_models() (per-model install_*.R).

Commands

Run from the repo root in R:

devtools::load_all()                       # load for development
devtools::document()                       # regenerate man/ and NAMESPACE (roxygen2 8.x)
devtools::test()                           # full suite (slow: builds and runs models)
devtools::test(filter = "build")           # one test file -> tests/testthat/test-build.R
testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-build.R")
devtools::check()                          # R CMD check (CI: windows-latest, release)
AEME::check_AEME_pkg()                     # end-to-end smoke test on the bundled example lake
pkgdown::build_site()                      # docs site (_pkgdown.yml controls the reference index)
  • tests/testthat/setup.R sets options(AEME.inform = FALSE, ncore = 2L) and pre-installs models once. helper-glm.R provides skip_if_models_unavailable(), skip_if_no_glm() and a model-subsetting helper; use these in new tests that need a model binary rather than adding OS checks.
  • Platform support: only glm_aed and simstrat_aed2 run on macOS/Linux; dy_cd and gotm_wet are Windows-only (see .windows_only_models in the test helper and .detect_os() in the package).
  • Suggests includes GitHub-only packages (aemetools, bathytools, ltapi; see Remotes). Parameter-sampling/calibration/sensitivity lives in aemetools, bathymetry processing in bathytools; don’t re-add that here (some helpers were recently moved into AEME from aemetools, see NEWS.md).

Architecture

The central object is the S4 class Aeme (R/Aeme.R, ~1800 lines: class, validity, accessors/setters, show). Its slots are lake, time, configuration, observations, input, inflows, outflows, water_balance, output, parameters. Accessor functions (lake(), time(), output(), …) and validObject() in the setters enforce structure, so go through accessors instead of @ where possible.

Typical pipeline (see README example):

  1. Load – yaml_to_aeme(path, "aeme.yaml") reads a lake description (plus observation/met/inflow/hypsograph files) into an Aeme object. Example lakes are in inst/extdata/ (lake, gotm_wet, …) and tests/testthat/LID45819_wainamu/.
  2. Build – build_aeme() (R/build_aeme.R) creates per-model config in path/<model>/ via the model-specific builders build_glm.R, build_dycd.R, build_gotm.R, build_simstrat.R. These call the many set_* functions (set_glm_*, set_gotm_*, set_dy_cd_*, set_simstrat_*, plus model-agnostic set_inflows, set_time, set_initial_conditions, …) and the writers (write_nml.R, write_yaml.R, make_dy_*.R, write_simstrat_nc.R). Model-specific file formats are handled by read_nml/nml_helpers, yaml for GOTM, plain text/cfg for DYRESM, JSON-like par for Simstrat.
  3. Parameters – input_model_parameters() / apply_parameters*.R map AEME’s generic parameter table (the parameters slot; columns defined in param_colnames.R) onto each model’s native parameter names. Parameter names/lookup tables are generated from data-raw/*.R + CSVs into data/ (sysdata/lazy data); edit the CSV and rerun the corresponding data-raw script rather than editing .rda files. Parameters are encoded as group/name[index] (encode_param()/decode_param()); zone-ratio/offset parameters are expanded in input_model_parameters().
  4. Run – run_aeme() (R/run_aeme.R) executes each model’s binary via processx (optionally parallel), then load_output() reads model-native output back into the output slot. run_aeme_ensemble() runs one model across many parameter sets, storing results as output(aeme)$ens_001.... write_aeme_parquet() / write_output_daily_nc.R export results.
  5. Analyse/plot – plot_*.R, summarise_aeme.R, get_var(), calc_*.R (met/heat-flux/water-balance helpers).

Cross-model variable mapping is central: AEME uses its own variable names (e.g. HYD_temp, HYD_wlev; see lookup_aeme_vars, guess_aeme_vars, key_naming.csv, generate_var_map_code.R) which are translated to each model’s native names on both write (set_output_vars, set_vars_sim) and read (load_output). When adding a variable or parameter you typically need to touch the lookup CSV/data-raw script and the per-model set/load code.

model_controls (get_model_controls(), model_controls_class.R, set_model_controls.R) toggles biogeochemistry and per-model options; use_bgc switches between physical-only and AED/WET/CAEDYM runs.

Conventions and gotchas

  • User-facing messages use cli; informational messages are gated on getOption("AEME.inform"). Model versions can be pinned with options such as AEME.glm_version, AEME.gotm_version, AEME.simstrat_version, AEME.simstrat_aed_version.
  • R/import-standalone-purrr.R is a vendored standalone file; don’t edit it by hand.
  • man/ and NAMESPACE are generated; edit roxygen comments in R/ and run document(). README.md is generated from README.Rmd.
  • Add a NEWS.md entry (top section is the in-development version) for user-visible changes.
  • Working branch is dev; PRs target dev/main. The repo root contains many scratch/output directories (aeme_tst, output, reprex*, test_write, models, etc.) and a stray nul file; these are not package source (check .Rbuildignore).
